claims.text: The untreated TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The untreated TiVNbTa alloy has an approximately 330 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
The untreated TiVNbTa alloy has an approximately 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain and 1273 K.
A controlled minor volume fraction of Y2O3 nanoparticles can be added during processing and distributed uniformly throughout TiVNbTa.
The added Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain dispersed at grain boundaries and within grain interiors.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will pin or obstruct dislocations in TiVNbTa at elevated temperature.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will impede grain-boundary sliding in TiVNbTa at elevated temperature.
Particle pinning by Y2O3 will stabilize the TiVNbTa microstructure at 1273 K.
Y2O3 dispersion strengthening will significantly increase the yield strength of TiVNbTa at 1273 K relative to the untreated alloy.
Y2O3 dispersion strengthening will significantly increase the compressive strength of TiVNbTa at 1273 K relative to the untreated alloy.
The modified alloy may approach or exceed 800 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
The modified alloy will maintain sufficient ductility while its elevated-temperature strength increases.
The proposed performance regime is sustained exposure at 1273 K under compressive deformation up to approximately 30% strain.
The proposed alloy is intended to function as a heat-transferring intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr.
A failure to achieve a statistically significant yield-strength improvement of at least 50% over 330 MPa would falsify the hypothesis.
